---
title: Run notebooks in the browser
description: Add run and download buttons to Python notebooks with JupyterLite and Pyodide.
order: 5
---

Readers can open a Python notebook in their browser with **Run in browser**.
JupyterLite supplies the notebook editor, and Pyodide runs Python in the browser.
The buttons and the loading page use the fonts and colours of your site.

Try the [plot example](browser-plot/index.ipynb) and the [data example](browser-data/index.ipynb).
The data example includes a CSV file and installs Seaborn from its generated dependency list.

## Turn on browser notebooks

Install the optional notebook support:

```bash
pip install 'smalldocs[notebooks]'
```

For a local checkout, use `uv sync --extra notebooks`.

Add this option to `_smalldocs.yml`:

```yaml
browser-notebooks: true
```

For `_quarto.yml`, put the option under `smalldocs`:

```yaml
smalldocs:
  browser-notebooks: true
```

Build your site with `smalldocs render`.
Each Python notebook that passes lint gets **Run in browser** and **Download and run** buttons.
The build creates the JupyterLite site in `lab/` and the bundles in `site_libs/notebooks/`.
Sites under a URL prefix use the same relative links.

## Packages and lint

smalldocs reads imports from the code cells and maps them to package names.
For example, `sklearn` becomes `scikit-learn`, and `PIL` becomes `pillow`.
Imports from the Python standard library do not need packages.

The build puts the package list into a copy of the notebook as PEP 723 metadata.
PEP 723 is a format for declaring Python dependencies in a comment block.
The source notebook stays unchanged.
When you run the copy in JupyterLite, its first code cell installs those packages.

Run the lint command on its own:

```bash
smalldocs notebooks lint docs
```

The lint checks for Python code and packages on a disallow list.
The list contains `torch`, `pytorch`, `pymc`, `pymc3`, `theano`, `theano-pymc` and `lxml`.
A notebook with one of those packages gets no run or download buttons.
The command reports each result and exits with code 1 if a notebook fails lint.

Lint does not execute the notebook or install its packages.
The check does not promise that every package or operation works in Pyodide.
Run the notebook yourself after you build the site.

To leave one notebook out, add this key to its front matter, the YAML cell at the start:

```yaml
browser-runnable: false
```

The same key works in the folder's `_metadata.yml`.
It can turn the runner off, but it cannot bypass the disallow list.

## Include data files

Keep each notebook in its own folder, with its files in `assets/` or `data/`:

```text
example/
  index.ipynb
  data/
    measurements.csv
```

The bundle includes images, CSV, TSV, JSON, text, NumPy arrays, pickle files and Python files in those folders.
Nested folders keep their paths, so `pandas.read_csv("data/measurements.csv")` reads the same file in JupyterLite.
The data example shows that layout.

Turning on browser notebooks publishes the notebook copies and their bundled files.
The notebook copies include hidden code cells.

## Open or download a notebook

Choose **Run in browser** to open a notebook in a new tab.
Use **Run > Run All Cells** in JupyterLite to install the packages and run the code.
Opening the runner again replaces that browser copy with the site's notebook.
Download your edits from JupyterLite before you reopen it.

Choose **Download and run** to save a ZIP file with the notebook and data.
Extract the ZIP, then run the notebook with `uvx juv run index.ipynb`.
`juv` reads the generated dependency metadata and installs the packages for desktop Python.

The build runs no notebook code.
Readers need an internet connection to download the browser's Python runtime and packages.
Serve the site over HTTPS, or use `smalldocs preview` on localhost.
